extracted.intended_audience: students, researchers, and general readers interested in rhetoric, media studies, and public apologies (particularly celebrity apologies)
extracted.subtask_description: Case-study analysis of a public apology (Michael Richards) that identifies rhetorical strategies used in the apology and provides transcript/sources for evaluation. Useful for studying apologia strategies and media responses to public scandals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mortification
rubrics_metrics.description: Admission of wrongdoing and explicit apology (taking responsibility and expressing remorse).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified on the page as one of the 'Key Apologia Strategies.' Demonstrated in Richards' statements: 'I lost my temper on stage... I’m really busted up over this and I’m very, very sorry to those people in the audience...' Use mortification when the speaker acknowledges the offense and issues a clear apology; evaluate sincerity, specificity, and whether responsibility is accepted rather than minimized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim that external provocation (e.g., heckling) caused or contributed to the offensive behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a 'Key Apologia Strategy.' Richards explicitly explains: 'I got heckled and I took it badly,' and repeatedly references being heckled during his act. When assessing provocation as a strategy, note whether the speaker is offering context (explanation) versus excusing/blaming others, and whether the provocation claim reduces perceived culpability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defeasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Assertion of lack of full information or lack of control at the time (spontaneity, inability to foresee or prevent the behavior).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Named among the 'Key Apologia Strategies.' Richards frames his actions as spontaneous performance behavior: 'I push the envelope, I work in a very uncontrolled manner onstage... I do a lot of free association, it’s spontaneous, I go into character.' Evaluate defeasibility claims by checking whether they admit fault while explaining limits to control, and whether they appear credible or merely evasive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation: Transcript and Sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide primary documentation of the apology (transcript/video) and contemporary news sources for context and verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page includes a 'Video Transcript' of Richards' Letterman appearance and lists news sources (Washington Post, TMZ, Fox News). As a rubric: include verbatim transcript excerpts and reputable sources when analyzing or presenting a public apology; use these to support claims about what was said, sequence of events, and public/media reaction.
